text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is defined as a reading of 130/80 mm Hg or higher.
Blood pressure is recorded as two numbers:

list.snippet: Systolic (top number): Pressure when the heart beats.
Diastolic (bottom number): Pressure when the heart rests between beats.

text_blocks.snippet: According to the American Heart Association and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, adult blood pressure falls into these ranges:

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

list.snippet: Elevated: Systolic between 120–129 and diastolic less than 80 mm Hg
Stage 1 Hypertension: Systolic between 130–139 or diastolic between 80–89 mm Hg
Stage 2 Hypertension: Systolic 140 mm Hg or higher or diastolic 90 mm Hg or higher
Hypertensive Crisis: Systolic over 180 and/or diastolic over 120 mm Hg (requires immediate medical care)
